1.title: Hit It, Pat!
1.topic: a child plays tee-ball at the park with Dad, misses the first swing, then hits the ball and runs to the base (sports, play, family, trying again)
sounds: Pat, bat, cap, Dad, bam, claps
입을 옆으로 크게 벌리고 '애': bat '뱃', cap '캡'. '밧', '캅'처럼 '아'가 되지 않게!
입을 살짝만 벌리고 짧게 '에': red '렛(드)', yet '옛'.
짧고 가볍게 '이': zips '집스', did '딧'. '이-'로 길게 늘이지 않아요.
1.expression: Sound proud on “Pat has a red bat,” say “Swish! Miss!” quickly like a fast swing, use a kind, cheering voice for “Not yet!”, say “Bam!” with a big pop, shout “Run, Pat, run!” like a coach, and finish with a happy “You did it!”

2.title: What Was That Noise?
2.topic: a boy hears a tapping noise at his window late at night, calls Dad, and they discover it is only a little branch blowing in the wind (feelings, family, night, humor)
sounds: walked, peeked, tapped, asked, laughed, tucked
k·p·f·s 소리 뒤 -ed는 짧은 't': walked '웍트', laughed '래프트'. '워키드'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
2.expression: Whisper “tap, tap, tap” slowly and spookily, sound scared and quick on “Dad! Something is at my window!”, slow down and get quiet on “They peeked outside together,” sound surprised and relieved on “Is that all?”, laugh a little, and say “Good night, branch!” in a sleepy, yawning voice.

3.title: Spiders: Amazing Web Builders
3.topic: how spiders (eight legs, not insects) spin orb webs from silk: a bridge thread on the wind, spokes, a sticky spiral, catching insects, and walking on the non-sticky lines (animals, science, nature)
lines: *Many* spiders *spin* *webs* | out of *silk* | that *comes* from their *bodies*. ↘
Spider *silk* is *thin*, | but it is *very* *strong* | and *stretchy*. ↘
When the *thread* *sticks* to a *branch*, | the spider has a *bridge*. ↘
When a *fly* *bumps* into the web, | it gets *stuck*! ↘
The spider *feels* the web *shake* | and *hurries* over for *dinner*. ↘
*Why* *doesn't* the spider get *stuck* *too*? ↘ | It *walks* *carefully* | on the lines that are *not* *sticky*. ↘
sounds: s와 p를 모음 없이 바로 붙여요: spin '스핀'이 아니라 's-pin' 한 박자로. '스'를 길게 내지 않아요.
s-t-r 세 소리를 한 번에: strong. '스트롱'처럼 '으'를 넣지 않고 빠르게 이어요.
혀끝을 윗니 사이로 살짝 내밀고 바람만 '쓰-': thin. '씬'이나 '틴'이 되지 않게!
3.expression: Read like a nature guide: sound sure on “Spiders are not insects,” stress the numbers “six” and “eight,” slow down on the steps “First … Next … Then,” sound excited on “it gets stuck!”, make “Why doesn't the spider get stuck too?” a curious question, and end gently but firmly on “please don't break it!”

4.title: Saturday at the Food Bank
4.topic: a boy who would rather play video games volunteers with his mom at a community food bank the Saturday before Thanksgiving, turns sorting cans into a race, hands a bag to a little girl and her grandpa, and asks to come back (community, holidays, helping, feelings)
lines: The *warehouse* was *huge*, | with *shelves* that *reached* *almost* to the *ceiling*. ↘
A *volunteer* named Ms. *Ortiz* | *handed* Marcus a *pair* of *gloves* | and *pointed* to a *mountain* of *boxes*. ↘
“Our *job* is to *sort* these *cans*,” she *explained*. | “*Soup* *here*, | *beans* *there*, | *vegetables* on this *table*.” ↘
At *first*, | the work felt *slow* and *boring*. | Marcus *kept* *checking* the *clock*. ↘
*Then* Ms. Ortiz *turned* it into a *race*. | “Let's *see* if your *table* can *beat* *mine*!” ↘
*Soon*, | Marcus was *sorting* *faster* than *ever*, | *calling* out “*Corn*!” and “*Peas*!” | as he *worked*. ↘
After *lunch*, | they *packed* the *cans* into *bags* | for *families* to *pick* *up*. ↘
When Marcus *gave* them a *bag*, | she *peeked* *inside* | and *whispered*, “*Thank* *you*.” ↘
sounds: 강세 없는 모음은 약하게 '어': com-MU-ni-ty '커뮤너티'. 모든 글자를 또박또박 읽지 않아요.
t·d 뒤는 '이드'(handed), 무성음 뒤는 't'(reached), 유성음 뒤는 'd'(explained).
끊지 말고 이어요: turned it into → '턴디린투', pick up → '피껍'.
4.expression: Sound grumpy in the first line, amazed at the huge warehouse, and friendly for Ms. Ortiz. Speed up during the race, soften for the girl's quiet “Thank you,” pause after “Suddenly,” ask “can we come back next month?” with hope, and make Mom's last line warm.
practice: Let's see if your table can beat mine!
I was hoping you would say that.
